scenarios.title: Plan designated roles through a router outage
scenarios.summary: Prepare a shared OSPF segment for a later high-priority router and the loss of the first designated router.
scenarios.objective: On a fresh Research segment, make North the designated router and West the backup. Set their priorities below Relay’s supplied priority. Keep Observer on the segment without allowing it to become a designated router or backup. Check that Relay’s later arrival leaves the incumbent roles in place, then verify that West takes over when North goes down.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: On a shared broadcast segment, OSPF chooses a designated router (DR) and a backup (BDR). An interface priority of zero excludes that router from those roles. It can still be an OSPF neighbor. For a fresh election among these supplied routers, the larger priority wins. If priorities tie, compare numerical Router IDs.
guide.action: Compare the settled roles on the supplied virtual segment.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: The priority determines eligibility and helps choose an open role. A router joining this established segment with a higher priority keeps the current DR and BDR in place. Compare a fresh election with a later arrival before planning any interruption.
guide.action: Compare the settled roles on the supplied virtual segment.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: If the DR goes down, the eligible BDR takes over and a new backup can be chosen. A pair of compatible routers involving a DR or BDR would attempt full adjacency. Two other routers can stay two-way neighbors. This exercise shows that decision from the settled roles.
guide.action: Compare the settled roles on the supplied virtual segment.

scenarios.retry_guidance: Check which routers are present and eligible at each stage.
hints: Set the observer’s interface priority so it remains a neighbor without being eligible.
Choose the fresh DR and BDR before comparing the late arrival.
The initial BDR is the first candidate to take over after the DR goes down.
scenarios.explanation: The fresh plan chooses North and West. Relay joins as a neighbor without displacing them. After North goes down, West takes over and Relay fills the backup role.
scenarios.simplifications: Known compatible two-way neighbors on one virtual broadcast segment with consistent settled roles. No packets, OSPF neighbor state machine, elections across differing declarations, LSA exchange, timer behavior, live convergence or real equipment.
